data.one_liner: Generates type‑safe Chopper client code from annotated service interfaces.
data.what_it_does: It reads Dart files with @ChopperApi annotations and produces .chopper.dart files containing request methods, serializers, and error handling. The generated code works with the Chopper runtime to perform HTTP calls.
use_when: You want compile‑time generated REST client code with minimal boilerplate
You already use the Chopper package for networking
You prefer strongly typed API interfaces over manual request building
avoid_when: You need a runtime‑only solution without build_runner
You prefer a different HTTP client API such as Dio or Retrofit
strengths: Reduces boilerplate by generating request code
Integrates tightly with Chopper’s interceptor and serialization system
Supports advanced features like query parameters and abortable requests
weaknesses: Only works with Chopper; not a standalone HTTP client
Generated code can be harder to debug than hand‑written requests
data.setup_notes: Add dev:chopper_generator and dev:build_runner to dev_dependencies, then run `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs`.

alternatives.name: retrofit
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides similar annotation‑based code generation for HTTP clients without needing Chopper

alternatives.name: dio
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers a powerful, hand‑coded HTTP client with interceptors and FormData support

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: Simple, low‑level HTTP client for cases where code generation is unnecessary
